images.alt:
The Nuggets’ last five wins have all been by single digits and they rank just 14th in point differential. But they’ve yet to lose two straight games, they’ve won three straight for the first time, and that includes their two best wins of the season. They came back from 17 points down to beat the Celtics on Wednesday and then ran past the Rockets in clutch time two nights later.

Two takeaways

Nuggets coach David Adelman has been leaning heavily on his starters. They played more than 25 minutes together in the win over Houston and almost 32 minutes together in their overtime win in Chicago on Sunday. For the season, the starters have played 60 more minutes (216) than any other lineup and have outscored their opponents by 14.5 points per 100 possessions, the third best mark among the 25 lineups that have played at least 75 minutes together.

The Nuggets have still seen the league’s sixth biggest drop in points scored per 100 possessions, in part because they had the league’s most efficient offense last season. But their last two games were the third and fourth times this season that they’ve scored more than 130 points per 100 possessions, something they did just twice before Thanksgiving last year.

Coming up: The Nuggets are the only team that has yet to have a back-to-back, and their first of 14 begins with their visit to Toronto on Sunday. They’re 4-0 against the Eastern Conference after their overtime win in Chicago over the weekend.
